subject: physics
examFormat: Physics is one of the three sections in the single combined EJU Science (理科) booklet; examinees choose 2 of the 3 subjects (physics/chemistry/biology) and answer them on a mark-sheet (one subject on the front side, one on the back). The whole booklet is timed at 80 minutes for the 2 chosen subjects. The physics section spans roughly pages 1-21 of the booklet and is organized into large blocks labeled with Roman numerals (typically I Mechanics, II Thermodynamics, III Waves, IV Electricity & Magnetism, V Atoms), each block containing several lettered sub-questions (A, B, C, ...) that map to numbered problems (問1, 問2, ...). There are 19 marked physics rows in recent papers (answer rows 1-19, with rows 20-75 left blank). Every question is single-best-answer multiple choice: a numbered prompt with a boxed answer-row number, choose ONE option, usually from 4-8 numbered choices. Choices are almost always symbolic algebraic expressions, ratios, numerical values, or selections among labeled diagrams/graphs (no free response, no working shown). The main text is Japanese; key technical terms and instructions for subject selection are bilingual (JP/EN). No calculator is allowed; arithmetic is kept light and answers are designed to be reached by reasoning and clean algebra. Gravitational acceleration is given as the symbol g, and air resistance is stated to be negligible unless noted.

questionArchetypes.description: Newton's-second-law / connected-bodies setup: two blocks in contact or masses connected over frictionless pulleys on an inclined plane; ask for the contact force ratio or the acceleration in terms of given masses and g. Answer is a symbolic expression or simple fraction of g.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Block A (mass m_A) is pushed by horizontal force F0 and pushes block B (mass m_B); A and B move together. Express the ratio F/F0 of the force A exerts on B. (2021_1 I-A)

questionArchetypes.description: Impulse-momentum theorem from a force-vs-time graph: a variable force acts for a finite time; read the area under the F-t graph to get the change in momentum or final speed.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: A constant-direction force F whose magnitude varies with t (given as an F-t graph) acts on a mass m initially at rest from t=0 to t=T. Find the speed v_T at t=T. (2021_1 I-B; same archetype 2020_2 I-C)

questionArchetypes.description: Collision with coefficient of restitution: 1-D collision of two bodies; combine momentum conservation and restitution (0<=e<=1) to bound or compute a post-collision velocity, or use post-collision sliding distances under friction to get a ratio in terms of e.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: On a frictionless line A (1.0 kg, 2.0 m/s) and B (1.0 kg, 1.0 m/s) move right and collide; afterward A moves at v_A. Since 0<=e<=1, find the minimum value of v_A. (2021_1 I-D)

questionArchetypes.description: Energy graph identification: a body oscillates/slides and you must pick which K(x) vs x graph (among 6 sketches) correctly shows kinetic energy as a spring contracts or a body moves, using energy conservation.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: A spring compressed by length L is released; choose the graph of kinetic energy K(x) versus compression x. (2021_1 I-E)

questionArchetypes.description: Circular / gravitation setup: object in uniform circular motion on a string of given geometry, or a satellite in circular or elliptical orbit; ask for tension, period, or a force/speed ratio using centripetal force, Kepler's laws, and energy/angular-momentum conservation.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: A mass m on a string (length l > h) anchored at height h does uniform circular motion of angular speed omega on the floor; express the string tension S. (2021_1 I-F). Also: satellite on an elliptical orbit, perigee distance 5R and perigee speed twice apogee speed; find ratio of gravitational force at apogee to that at the surface. (2020_2 I-F)

questionArchetypes.description: Calorimetry / heat-of-fusion mixing: mix water and ice (or water and a metal/container of given heat capacity); use conservation of heat with specific heats and latent heat to find remaining ice mass or final temperature.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: 120 g of water at 20C plus 40 g of ice at -10C reach 0C; given c_water, c_ice, and heat of fusion, find the mass of ice remaining. (2021_1 II-A; container variant 2020_2 II-A, 2018_2 II-A)

questionArchetypes.description: p-V diagram reasoning: a gas is taken between two states by different paths (isobaric/isothermal/adiabatic); rank the absorbed heats Q for the paths, or identify which processes decrease internal energy, or compute net heat absorbed over a cycle/path using the first law.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: An ideal gas goes from A to B via three paths I, II, III on a p-V diagram; rank Q_I, Q_II, Q_III. (2021_1 II-C). Also: which processes decrease internal energy among isobaric/adiabatic legs (2020_2 II-C).

questionArchetypes.description: Sinusoidal wave from a graph: given a y-x snapshot (and sometimes a y-t graph) for a wave of stated frequency/direction, find the first time the displacement at a point becomes maximum, sketch the wave at a later time, or write the wave equation y=A sin(...).
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: A 10 Hz sine wave travels in +x; given the t=0 displacement graph, find the first time t1 at which y at x=10.0 cm is positive maximum. (2021_1 III-A; wave-equation variant 2020_2 III-A; later-time-graph variant 2019_1 III-A)

questionArchetypes.description: String/air-column resonance scaling: fundamental frequency of a string depends on tension^(1/2) and linear-density^(-1/2) and length; change tension/length and equate frequencies to find a length or tension ratio. Air-column variant uses number of antinodes n.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Two strings of equal length a have matched fundamentals; A's tension is multiplied by s and B's length changed to b, keeping fundamentals equal; express s. (2021_1 III-B; air-column open-pipe variant 2019_1 III-B)

questionArchetypes.description: Refraction / total reflection through layered media: light passes air-glass-glass or water-glass-air with given refractive indices; apply Snell's law across boundaries to find sin(theta) of the refracted ray or the critical angle, or find an unknown refractive index from a critical-angle geometry.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Light enters glass A (n=1.7) from air at 60 deg then refracts into glass B (n=1.5) at angle theta; find sin(theta). (2021_1 III-C; critical-angle variants 2020_2 III-C and 2019_1 III-C)

questionArchetypes.description: Doppler effect with both source and observer moving: source emits f0 while moving; observer ahead measures f1 and behind measures f2; express the ratio f2/f1 in terms of V, v_S, v_O.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: A source emitting f0 moves at v_S; an observer moving at v_O is ahead (measures f1) then behind (measures f2). Express f2/f1. (2018_2 III-B)

questionArchetypes.description: Point charges in a geometric arrangement: charges fixed at the corners of a square/cube or on an axis; find the charge Q (or ratio Q/q) that makes the net electrostatic force on one charge zero, or find the potential at the center, or locate where the field is zero on an axis.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Charges q, 2q, 2q sit at three corners of a square ABCD; a charge Q at the fourth corner makes the force on the q charge zero. Find Q/q. (2021_1 IV-A; field-zero-location variant 2019_1 IV-A; cube-center potential 2020_2 IV-B)

questionArchetypes.description: Capacitor energy / Joule heat on switching: capacitors with initial charge are reconnected through a resistor by closing a switch; using charge redistribution and energy conservation, find the Joule heat dissipated in the resistor, or the final charge on a plate.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Capacitor C carries charge Q, capacitor 2C is uncharged; closing switch S lets current flow through R until it stops. Find the total Joule heat in R. (2021_1 IV-B; charging-heat variant 2019_1 IV-D)

questionArchetypes.description: DC circuit comparison / power: equal resistors arranged two different ways with an ideal battery; find the ratio of total power consumed, or the current through a specific resistor, or power dissipated in an unknown resistor given a branch current.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Three equal resistors plus a battery are wired as in Fig 1 (total power P1) then as in Fig 2 (total power P2); find P1/P2. (2021_1 IV-C; current-through-R variant 2020_2 IV-D; two-battery Kirchhoff branch-current/direction 2018_2 IV-C)

questionArchetypes.description: Magnetic field from parallel currents / force on a current: two or three long straight wires carry currents; find the point where the net field is zero (ratio d/a), or the magnitude and direction of the field at a point, or the net force on one wire from the others.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Wires at x=-a (current I) and x=a (current 2I) both out of the page; the field is zero at x=d. Find d/a. (2021_1 IV-D; three-wire field-at-corner variant 2019_1 IV-E; three-wire force variant 2018_2 IV-D)

questionArchetypes.description: Force balance with magnetic force, or charged particle in a field: a current-carrying conductor hangs in a field and you find the flux density from the equilibrium angle; or a charged particle enters a field region and you find where it exits / the radius-vs-B relationship.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: A conducting rod QR (mass m, length l) hangs by wires carrying current I in an upward field and rests at angle theta from vertical; express the flux density. (2021_1 IV-E; particle-exit-point variant 2020_2 IV-E; r-vs-B graph 2019_1 IV-F; landing x-coordinate and time 2018_2 IV-E)

questionArchetypes.description: Electromagnetic induction direction & force: a coil or loop moves near a magnet, or the field through a fixed loop changes with time (given a B-t graph); determine the induced-current direction and the direction/graph of the force, using Lenz's and Faraday's laws.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: A square coil moves at speed v away from the point below a bar magnet (N pole down); state the induced-current direction (CW/CCW) and the direction of the force on the coil. (2021_1 IV-F; F_x vs t graph from a B-t graph 2020_2 IV-F; rail/rod acceleration reasoning 2018_2 IV-F)

questionArchetypes.description: Nuclear reaction / atomic single-question (block V usually has just one item): balance a fission or decay reaction (count emitted neutrons), relate de Broglie wavelength to kinetic energy, identify quark charges, or relate photon/electron energy to wavelength dependence.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: U-235 absorbs a neutron and fissions into Xe-140 and Sr-94; how many neutrons are released? (2021_1 V-A). Also: express kinetic energy K in terms of de Broglie wavelength lambda (2020_2 V-A); charge of a down quark in terms of e (2019_1 V-A).

styleNotes: Generate single-best-answer multiple-choice items grouped under the five Roman-numeral blocks (I Mechanics ~6 items, II Thermodynamics 3, III Waves 3, IV Electricity & Magnetism 6, V Atoms 1), matching the ~19-question recent layout. Each item is a short physics scenario followed by 'choose the correct one from 1-N' with 4-8 options. Prefer SYMBOLIC answers (algebraic expressions, ratios like a/b, fractions of g, or clean numerical values reachable without a calculator); avoid messy decimals. Use given constants/symbols rather than numbers where possible: gravitational acceleration g, Coulomb constant k, Planck constant h, elementary charge e; explicitly state 'air resistance negligible', 'frictionless', 'light/inextensible string', 'ideal gas', 'monatomic gas' as appropriate. Heavily favor these recurring formats: read a quantity off a graph (F-t, v-t, p-V, y-x, y-t, B-t) and apply a theorem; equilibrium/ratio problems with masses and angles; choosing among 6 candidate graphs or among labeled diagram options; and 'find the value that makes X equal to zero'. Keep arithmetic light (nice numbers: 30 deg, 45 deg, 60 deg, factors of 2, sqrt(2), sqrt(3)). One combined idea per item; difficulty is solid first-year-university entrance level (standard Japanese high-school 'Advanced Physics'), conceptually clean but requiring correct setup. Write stems in Japanese with bilingual technical terms where natural; options are mathematical, so language-neutral. Include a diagram description in words since figures are part of most items.
